question: the prompt cache held ~8 GB of system RAM on a machine whose GPU carve leaves 31.6 GB, and a long conversation was being prefilled again even though its state was on disk
method: tmp/cache_ram_probe.py: the build under test against a SHADOW cache directory of hardlinks (same volume, so nothing the scan removes touches the real entries), 4 slots at ctx 262144, vision off. Two cached conversations are replayed by the token ids stored in their own .spc files, so no re-tokenisation drift; the load time comes from the server log, the memory from the process. STRIX_PROBE_EXE=app runs the runtime the installed 0.1.5 ships, STRIX_NO_MTP=1 repeats it with MTP off, STRIX_CACHE_RAM overrides the limit.

system_ram.cause: --cache-ram defaults to 8192 MiB and tools/manager.py never passed it. The KV cache itself lives in the GPU carve; this was the RAM tier of the server's prompt cache, and it is what came back when the model was unloaded.
system_ram.measured: controlled A/B, same build, one slot, four cached conversations replayed in sequence so each eviction goes through the save path: llama-server resident 8.07 GB at --cache-ram 8192 against 4.13 GB at 1024 (1.78 GB after load in both). The remaining 4 GB is the restored conversation own checkpoints held by the slot plus the read buffers, not the cache tier. Matches what the live app showed: 7.1 GB with three conversations cached, and about 8 GB returned when the model was unloaded. Private commit reads ~80 GB in Task Manager either way: that is the GPU carve, not system memory.
system_ram.why it needed more than the flag: server_prompt_cache::alloc() returns nullptr for a state larger than the RAM limit, and persist() only ever ran on a state alloc() had accepted. A small --cache-ram would therefore have stopped every long conversation from reaching the disk tier - the tier that exists for exactly those. persist() now takes (prompt, main, drft) and prompt_save() gathers into a temporary when the RAM tier declines.
system_ram.setting: PROMPT_CACHE_RAM_MIB = 1024 in tools/manager.py. A conversation of this model is ~55-128 KB per token with checkpoints, so 1 GiB holds roughly a 10K-token chat and everything longer goes to disk alone.
system_ram.it also got faster: the same four replays took 83.4 s of request time at 8192 and 57.5 s at 1024, because the disk reads stop competing with the cache for memory: the 5.630 GiB entry 25.9 s -> 18.9 s
system_ram.regression checked: STRIX_GENERATE=40 grows each conversation past every stored entry so the save path has something new to write. With --cache-ram 1024 the server still wrote 2.006 GiB and 5.741 GiB states to disk, which is exactly what alloc() would have refused before persist() was decoupled from it. When the disk already holds the same conversation, disk_wants() skips the write - the old path re-wrote 2.0 GB and 5.7 GB for nothing.

disk_tier_selection.defect: load_from_disk ranked candidates the way the RAM tier does, requiring f_keep to strictly increase. A short entry that is a complete prefix reaches f_keep = 1.000, after which no longer entry can ever exceed it, so it shadows the rest of the same conversation for good.
disk_tier_selection.measured: asking for the 79441-token conversation picked the 49370-token entry (f_keep = 1.000, f_sim = 0.621) and prefilled 30071 tokens: 46.3 s. Ranking by the tokens actually skipped, with f_keep >= 0.25 and f_sim above the running base as the guards, takes the 79441 entry (f_keep = 1.000, f_sim = 1.000) and prefills 2897: 17.3 s. Cold, that prompt is 96.6 s.
disk_tier_selection.the other conversation: 36311 tokens: 43.8 s cold, 8.3-9.1 s from disk (2551 tokens prefilled)

mtp_and_the_cache.defect: an entry written with MTP on carries the draft model state. Reopening it with MTP off left ctx_dft null and hit GGML_ASSERT(ctx_dft) in server_prompt_cache::load, killing the server: the whole of the 2026-09-21 19:08 session, 56 s from start to abort, immediately after "disk cache: read 63015 tokens, 3.412 GiB".
mtp_and_the_cache.fix: the two directions are not symmetric. MTP off with a draft state present is fine - nothing drafts, so the target state is complete and the draft half is dropped with a log line. MTP on with no draft state is not: the draft context would hold no cells for a sequence the target is already deep into, so the entry is refused and the prompt is processed.
mtp_and_the_cache.verified: STRIX_NO_MTP=1 replays both conversations against entries written with MTP on: both hit at f_keep = f_sim = 1.000, the server survives, and the log says it kept the target state

read_speed.measured: the server reads a 1.895 GiB entry in 3.8-4.2 s and a 5.630 GiB entry in 12.1 s. A plain sequential read of the same file on the same drive is 1.0-1.4 s for 1.9 GiB (1411-1864 MB/s, Crucial P310 NVMe).
read_speed.reading: the gap is the buffers, not the drive: every blob is a fresh std::vector that is zero-filled and then overwritten, and the first touch faults in multiple GB of new commit. Lower memory pressure from --cache-ram 1024 helps; a no-init buffer or a chunked restore would be the next step, worth roughly 3 s on a 1.9 GiB entry and 7 on a 5.6 GiB one.

not_a_defect: the directory looked like it held 13 entries / 18.9 GiB while the server indexed 8 / 15.2 GiB. The five extra files are in the Claude sandbox overlay (AppData/Local/Packages/Claude_*/LocalCache/...), written when the app was launched from inside the sandbox on 2026-09-21; a shell inside the sandbox sees a merged view, and llama-server outside it sees only the real directory. The index is correct. Those 3.7 GiB are stranded and can be deleted by hand.
ceiling: the 16 GiB limit is now the profile field prompt_cache_disk_mib (1024-262144 MiB), since a single 79K-token conversation is 5.6 GiB and three of them filled it
